Exercise: Low Pulley Row To Neck

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- compound

Primary Muscles:

- shoulders

Secondary Muscles:

- biceps
- middle back
- traps

Equipment:

- cable

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1.5 hours

Goals:

- hypertrophy
- strength

Contraindications:

- condition: Shoulder Injury, description: Individuals with shoulder injuries should avoid this exercise or modify the movement to reduce stress on the shoulders.
- condition: Lower Back Pain, description: Individuals experiencing lower back pain may need to adjust their posture and ensure proper form to prevent exacerbation of symptoms.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Wide Grip Low Pulley Row To Neck, force: pull, level: intermediate, mechanic: compound, primaryMuscles: ['shoulders'], secondaryMuscles: ['biceps', 'middle back', 'traps']

Substitution Options:

- name: Dumbbell Row, equipment: dumbbells
- name: Barbell Bent Over Row, equipment: barbell

Instructions:

- Sit on a low pulley row machine with a rope attachment.
- Grab the ends of the rope using a palms-down grip and sit with your back straight and your knees slightly bent. Tip: Keep your back almost completely vertical and your arms fully extended in front of you. This will be your starting position.
- While keeping your torso stationary, lift your elbows and start bending them as you pull the rope towards your neck while exhaling. Throughout the movement your upper arms should remain parallel to the floor. Tip: Continue this motion until your hands are almost next to your ears (the forearms will not be parallel to the floor at the end of the movement as they will be angled a bit upwards) and your elbows are out away from your sides.
- After holding for a second or so at the contracted position, come back slowly to the starting position as you inhale. Tip: Again, during no part of the movement should the torso move.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
